Without the answer options, I'd pick **palpation of the jugular venous pulse** as the unnecessary step, because the JVP is assessed by inspection. Positioning the patient at about 30–45° with the head turned slightly away, good lighting, and measuring the height above the sternal angle (adding 5 cm to estimate right atrial pressure) are all standard parts of the exam. If your list had different options, paste them and I'll check against those.
